newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel beefs up security, arrests Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel beefs up security, arrests Palestinians.

text.p: Israel tightened security in its cities on Friday and pressed ahead with a crackdown on Islamic militant groups it says may have launched the double suicide bombing which ripped throught Jerusalem's main Jewish market.

A senior Palestinian official hit back at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, insisting the PLO had acted to prevent violence but that his right-wing government had done its best to scrap peace.

In Washington, President Bill Clinton put an end to speculation that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright could come to the region as soon as next week to try to rescue the peace process in the wake of the bombings.
He said Albright would visit only after a preparatory trip by his Middle East envoy, Dennis Ross.

The Israeli army said it had rounded up another 51 West Bank Palestinians overnight, bringing to 79 the total number of alleged militants it has arrested since two bombers killed 13 people, ranging in age from 15 to 92, in Wednesday's attack.

"Since our working assumptions are that Hamas or Islamic Jihad stand behind this attack, we are arresting whatever in an investigation can help us solve the attack," the army chief, Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak, told reporters.

In Jerusalem, police and paramilitary troops beefed up security as a precaution against any further bloodshed. Islamist militants have in the past carried out a series of suicide bombings over several days.

"We have deployed several hundred additional police, border police and soldiers to secure major centres. There are roving patrols, we put up barricades within the city and intelligence activities are ongoing," police spokesman Shmulik Ben-Ruby said.

A leaflet issued on Wednesday in the name of Hamas's military brigades claimed responsibility for the attack and gave Israel until 9 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Sunday to free all Palestinian prisoners. Israeli officials are not sure of its authenticity.
A Hamas leaflet issued on Friday praised the attack and hailed resistance as the only way to liberate the land. But it did not claim responsibility or repeat the ultimatum.
Netanyahu has accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of doing "damn all" to prevent violence.

He has suspended peace talks with the Palestinians, imposed a total closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip and aides have threatened that Israeli forces would re-enter PLO-ruled areas to seize "terrorists" if Arafat failed to do the job.
Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo said the moves were "aimed at weakening Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and his Authority rather than aimed at fighting terrorism".
"During the recent months and weeks, we have prevented many incidents and terrorist acts to ensure security and peace," Abed Rabbo told a news conference in Ramallah.
"But Netanyahu was exerting maximum effort to demolish Palestinian houses, build settlements and undermine peace."

Arafat convened his cabinet on Friday for the first time since the attack and since the Palestinian Legislative Council voted this week to urge he dissolve his cabinet and appoint a new one with "qualified and experienced ministers" by September.
The council's recommendation, over alleged corruption and mismanagement, has added to the pressures on the Palestinian leader.
Palestinian forces have also made arrests since Wednesday's attack. In Gaza, PLO forces freed two senior Hamas political leaders after questioning them for three hours.

Police eliminated suspicions that the bombers were two young men missing for 14 months from their homes in the West Bank village of Dahariyeh. Genetic tests on relatives showed they were not the attackers, police said.
Despite a block on Israeli-Palestinian peace moves, the Israeli army chief said the two sides were engaged in security "coordination of various sorts" to try to crack the case.

A Palestinian official said a meeting of Israeli and PLO officers on Thursday night had cleared the way for an easing of the closure that Israel clamped on the West Bank and Gaza Strip barring Arabs from entering the Jewish state.
The army said entry would be allowed in medical emergencies and for medical personnel in Arab East Jerusalem.
Wednesday's attack deepened a four-month peace crisis sparked in March when Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.
